title: Boss: the dry run that deleted everything
summary: A remote clean-up whose -DryRun wiped every log, a cache warmer that gets itself rate-limited, and a script that only works where someone once typed Set-Secret.

steps.title: Incident review INC-5120
body: *"An engineer ran `clean-remote.ps1 -DryRun` on staging to preview it. It deleted every log on both web servers,
including today's. The same week the post-deploy cache warm-up reported half its pages failed, and the new CI capacity
check fails with an error nobody understands."*
The staging logs have been restored on web01 and web02. **Read the script before you run it.** Every check
restores the folder first and then runs your fixed script.

steps.title: -DryRun deleted everything
prompt: Read `~/scripts/clean-remote.ps1` (`Get-Content`). Work out why `-DryRun` deleted files, and why it deleted **all**
of them, not only those older than `-Days`.
Fix it, so that `-DryRun` deletes nothing and a real run deletes only files older than `-Days` (default 30) on
every server. If you test it for real and lose the files, `cp -a /opt/dojo/state/srvlogs/. /srv/logs/app/` puts them back.

checks.name: -DryRun deletes nothing
checks.cmd: rm -rf /srv/logs/app/*; cp -a /opt/dojo/state/srvlogs/. /srv/logs/app/; timeout 60 pwsh -NoProfile -NonInteractive -File ~/scripts/clean-remote.ps1 -DryRun >/dev/null 2>&1; ls /srv/logs/app | tr '\n' ' '
checks.expectOutput: api-1.log api-2.log api-3.log api-4.log worker.log worker.log.1
checks.fail: With `-DryRun`, all six files must still be there.

checks.name: a real run deletes only the old files
checks.cmd: rm -rf /srv/logs/app/*; cp -a /opt/dojo/state/srvlogs/. /srv/logs/app/; timeout 60 pwsh -NoProfile -NonInteractive -File ~/scripts/clean-remote.ps1 >/dev/null 2>&1; ls /srv/logs/app | tr '\n' ' '
checks.fail: Without `-DryRun`, only the files older than 30 days (`api-3.log`, `api-4.log`, `worker.log.1`) should go.

checks.name: -Days is honoured remotely
checks.cmd: rm -rf /srv/logs/app/*; cp -a /opt/dojo/state/srvlogs/. /srv/logs/app/; timeout 60 pwsh -NoProfile -NonInteractive -File ~/scripts/clean-remote.ps1 -Days 10 >/dev/null 2>&1; ls /srv/logs/app | tr '\n' ' '; rm -rf /srv/logs/app/*; cp -a /opt/dojo/state/srvlogs/. /srv/logs/app/
checks.fail: With `-Days 10`, `api-1.log` and `worker.log` should be all that is left.

hints: The script block runs on the servers, in a new session. What are `$Days` and `$DryRun` there?
Both are `$null` remotely: `AddDays(-$null)` is *now* (so every file is "old"), and `-WhatIf:$null` means "not a dry run". Use `$using:`.
solution: # clean-remote.ps1: deletes old app logs on every web server. -DryRun shows what would go.
explain: Two missing `$using:` turned a preview into a wipe. The habits that would each have stopped it: `Set-StrictMode
-Version Latest` *inside* the remote block (reading an unset `$Days` throws), a dry run whose output you read before
the real run (it listed every file, today's included), and a Pester test that runs the script with `-DryRun` and

steps.title: Half the pages failed to warm
prompt: Run `pwsh -File ~/scripts/warm-cache.ps1`. It requests 30 pages in parallel and reports how many failed. Find out why
they fail (call one URL yourself with 30 others in flight, or look at the status code of a failure), then fix the
script so it prints **`warmed 30, failed 0`** in under 15 seconds. The API allows 8 concurrent requests.

checks.name: warmed 30, failed 0, quickly
checks.cmd: s=$(date +%s); out=$(timeout 40 pwsh -NoProfile -NonInteractive -File ~/scripts/warm-cache.ps1 2>&1 | tr -d '\r'); t=$(( $(date +%s) - s )); echo "$out (${t}s)"; test "$out" = 'warmed 30, failed 0' && test $t -lt 15
checks.fail: The script should print `warmed 30, failed 0` and take less than 15 seconds.

hints: Change the `catch` to print `$_.Exception.Response.StatusCode` once: the failures are `429 Too Many Requests`.
`-ThrottleLimit 30` sends all 30 at once; the API allows 8. Lower it (6 to 8).
For safety, also let each call retry: `Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $_ -TimeoutSec 5 -MaximumRetryCount 3 -RetryIntervalSec 1`.
steps.explain: More threads is not more speed once the other side says no. A 429 (with its `Retry-After` header) is the server telling you its limit; respect it with a throttle below the limit and retries for the occasional rejection. Against shared production services, agree the limit with the team that runs them.

steps.title: There are currently no extension vaults registered
prompt: Run `pwsh -File ~/scripts/ci-ticket-count.ps1`. It works on the admin's laptop, where a vault holds `OpsApiToken`;
this machine is like a CI agent: **no vault**. CI systems hand secrets to jobs as **environment variables** (masked in
- when **`$env:OPS_API_TOKEN`** is set, it uses that (and does not touch SecretManagement);
- when neither works, it stops with a clear error that mentions **`OPS_API_TOKEN`**, and exits non-zero.
Test it with `$env:OPS_API_TOKEN = Get-Content /opt/dojo/state/api-token` (in a real pipeline, the secret variable does this).

checks.name: works with OPS_API_TOKEN
checks.fail: With `OPS_API_TOKEN` set, the script should print `tickets: 47`.

checks.name: a clear error without it
checks.cmd: out=$(env -u OPS_API_TOKEN pwsh -NoProfile -NonInteractive -File ~/scripts/ci-ticket-count.ps1 2>&1); rc=$?; echo "$out" | tail -n 3; test $rc -ne 0 && echo "$out" | grep -q OPS_API_TOKEN
checks.fail: Without the variable and without a vault, the script must exit non-zero with a message that mentions `OPS_API_TOKEN`.

checks.name: no token in the script
checks.fail: Never paste the token into the script.

hints: In the `else`: `try { $token = Get-Secret -Name OpsApiToken -AsPlainText } catch { throw "No API token: set OPS_API_TOKEN or store OpsApiToken with Set-Secret ($($_.Exception.Message))" }`.
Replace the `$token = Get-Secret ...` line with that block.
solution: catch { throw "No API token: set the OPS_API_TOKEN variable (CI) or store OpsApiToken with Set-Secret. ($($_.Exception.Message))" }
explain: One script, two worlds: interactive machines with a vault, pipelines with injected variables. The error message is
part of the fix: the next person to see it learns what to configure instead of reading SecretManagement's
internals. Never `Write-Output` the token to check it: pipelines mask known secrets in logs, but only exact matches.
